findings.title: A same-user process can open the Windows worker before its access lists are set
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Start a worker on Windows; from another process of the same user, call OpenProcess with PROCESS_VM_READ on it before it isolates itself.
findings.expected: No process other than the parent can open the worker for memory access at any time.
findings.observed: CreateProcessW received null security attributes; the restricted list came later, and a new list does not revoke an open handle.
findings.impact: The other process keeps PROCESS_VM_READ and reads the worker's memory, the secret included.
findings.recommendedFix: Create the worker with its access lists, or suspended and restricted before it runs.
findings.requiredVerification: A native Windows test that opens the new process for memory reading and is refused.

findings.title: A macOS terminal worker can type into the user's shell and change other terminals
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: From compromised code in a terminal worker on macOS, call ioctl(TIOCSTI) on the terminal, or open another /dev/ttysN for writing or chmod it.
findings.expected: A sandboxed worker cannot make anything outside the sandbox run and cannot change other terminals.
findings.observed: The profile granted file-write* and file-ioctl on every terminal; the terminal worker kept its controlling terminal and an inherited standard error.
findings.impact: A command typed into the user's shell runs outside the sandbox after the program exits; fake prompts and mode changes on other terminals.
findings.recommendedFix: No controlling terminal for any worker; the terminal descriptor only; data writes and ioctls on the own terminal's path only.
findings.requiredVerification: TIOCSTI from a worker on a pseudo-terminal is refused and no input arrives.

findings.title: Linux enters the user namespace before it forbids reading its memory
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: While a process isolates itself, keep opening /proc/<pid>/mem from another process of the user with ptrace_scope=1.
findings.expected: No other process of the user can open the memory at any point of the isolation.
findings.observed: unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) ran before PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0; in the user's own namespace every process of the user holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE, which passes Yama.
findings.impact: The other process keeps a descriptor to the memory while NoMemoryReading reads Confirmed.
findings.recommendedFix: Clear the dumpable flag and the core limit before the namespace step.
findings.requiredVerification: The isolation clears the flag before unshare.

findings.title: Worker start and calls can block without end
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Start a worker whose start stalls, or call one whose handler never returns.
findings.expected: The caller can bound the wait and get control back.
findings.observed: No deadline and no cancellation.
findings.impact: The calling thread hangs; no secret leaves the worker.
findings.recommendedFix: Deadlines with one clear lifecycle.
findings.requiredVerification: A call past its deadline fails in bounded time and leaves no usable worker.

findings.title: enter_requiring accepts protection confirmed for one thread
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Call Isolation::enter_requiring with a protection confirmed only for the calling thread.
findings.expected: A caller can require every thread without reading each measure.
findings.observed: A thread-scoped Confirmed outcome passes.
findings.impact: A caller can believe a restriction covers the process when it covers one thread.
findings.recommendedFix: A fail-closed variant such as enter_requiring_process_wide.
findings.requiredVerification: A thread-scoped outcome fails the process-wide rule.

findings.title: A release does not wait for the full test matrix, fuzzing and the advisory check
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Push a release tag.
findings.expected: Packaging waits for the native tests, fuzzing and RustSec on the tagged commit.
findings.observed: Packaging ran independently of them.
findings.impact: The attestation proves origin, not acceptance on the supported platforms.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the release depend on the full acceptance matrix and the advisory check.
findings.requiredVerification: The packaging job needs the test, audit and fuzz jobs.

findings.title: SignalsToSelfOnly passes signals sent through fcntl ownership
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: With signals_to_self_only, set F_SETOWN or F_SETOWN_EX to another process and O_ASYNC on a descriptor.
findings.expected: No signal reaches another process.
findings.observed: The kernel signals any process or group of the user; sigio_perm checks only user IDs.
findings.impact: Another process of the user can be killed.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse fcntl commands 8 and 15 with the option.
findings.requiredVerification: Both commands are refused with EACCES under the option.

findings.title: A deadline can be lost: an unrepresentable one and the Unix launch wait
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Call start_within or call_within with Duration::MAX, or let posix_spawn stall under start_within on Unix.
findings.expected: The deadline bounds every wait, or the contract says where it does not.
findings.observed: checked_add gives no deadline for an unrepresentable Duration; the Unix launch ignored the deadline.
findings.impact: A caller can wait longer than the deadline it gave.
findings.recommendedFix: Bound or refuse such a Duration and the launch wait, or document them.
findings.requiredVerification: A start with a zero deadline fails with TimedOut; the documentation states the unrepresentable case.

findings.title: The README describes the terminal worker, installation and coverage wrongly
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Read the README against the code.
findings.expected: The README matches the code and links its evidence.
findings.observed: It promised a controlling terminal, named only a Git dependency and gave coverage without its revision and report.
findings.impact: Readers rely on behaviour the crate no longer has.
findings.recommendedFix: Bring the README in line (DOC-06 to DOC-09).
findings.requiredVerification: The README matches the code.

findings.title: Third-party notices name older versions than the lockfile
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Compare the notices with Cargo.lock.
findings.expected: The notices name the locked versions.
findings.observed: They named zeroize 1.9.1 and landlock 0.4.7; the lock holds 1.9.2 and 0.4.8.
findings.impact: An inaccurate dependency inventory.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the notices and check them.
findings.requiredVerification: CI compares the notices with the dependency tree.

findings.title: Compatible version ranges can resolve to untested versions
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Build a program with a newer release of one of the dependencies.
findings.expected: The program uses the tested versions.
findings.observed: Compatible ranges let a program resolve newer releases than the tested Cargo.lock.
findings.impact: Untested dependency versions at run time.
findings.recommendedFix: Document the ranges and the tested lockfile.
findings.requiredVerification: The documentation names the tested lockfile.

findings.title: FileLocksRefused leaves leases open
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: With refuse_file_locks, call fcntl(F_SETLEASE).
findings.expected: Leases are refused as locks are.
findings.observed: F_SETLEASE was allowed.
findings.impact: A one-bit channel through /proc/locks and stalled opens.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse F_SETLEASE with the option.
findings.requiredVerification: Refused with EACCES under the option.

findings.title: The filter allows calls that act on other processes
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: After isolation, call prlimit64, setpriority, sched_setaffinity, ioprio_set or move_pages on another process of the user.
findings.expected: Calls on other processes are refused, as the filter's description says.
findings.observed: They stayed allowed; PR_SET_NAME sets a name anyone reads.
findings.impact: Raised core limits of another process, renicing, page-residency probes.
findings.recommendedFix: Check the process argument or narrow the description.
findings.requiredVerification: Calls on another process are refused and those on the process itself work.

findings.title: The kernel can copy secret pages and free the old ones unwiped
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Let khugepaged collapse a work area or stack, or compaction move locked pages.
findings.expected: Secret pages are not copied behind the program's back, or the residue is documented.
findings.observed: Work areas and stacks lacked MADV_NOHUGEPAGE; compaction moves locked pages by default.
findings.impact: Old copies of secret bytes in freed pages.
findings.recommendedFix: Small pages for stacks; document the residue; recommend init_on_free=1.
findings.requiredVerification: Stacks ask for small pages; the residue is documented.

findings.title: A worker is started from the program path, looked up again
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Replace the program file while the program runs, then start a worker.
findings.expected: A worker runs the same program as its parent.
findings.observed: The path was looked up at each start.
findings.impact: A replaced file receives the secrets.
findings.recommendedFix: On Linux, start /proc/self/exe.
findings.requiredVerification: Linux starts /proc/self/exe; the documentation names the other systems.

findings.title: The macOS sandbox grants /dev/tty to a process without a terminal
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Isolate a process on macOS whose standard streams are redirected but which keeps a controlling terminal.
findings.expected: A process without a terminal among its streams gets no terminal rule.
findings.observed: profile() always allowed /dev/tty.
findings.impact: TIOCSTI through /dev/tty stays possible.
findings.recommendedFix: Add /dev/tty only with an own terminal.
findings.requiredVerification: The profile has no terminal rule without one.

findings.title: Public fields of Isolation can drift from its outcomes
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
findings.reproduction: Change a public bool field of an Isolation.
findings.expected: Fields and outcomes agree.
findings.observed: has and require read the outcomes, not the fields.
findings.impact: A caller reading a changed field sees another state than the checks.
findings.recommendedFix: Read-only accessors.
findings.requiredVerification: The documentation states that the fields are a copy and no check reads them.

findings.title: Two files exceed 800 lines of code (CORE-15)
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Count the lines of code.
findings.expected: At most 800 per file, or an exception with its reason.
findings.observed: 810 and 887 lines of code.
findings.impact: Harder review.
findings.recommendedFix: Split by responsibility.
findings.requiredVerification: Both files are under 800 lines of code.

findings.title: Duplicated declarations and a descriptor parsed again per thread (CORE-10)
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Read the declarations and the Windows thread walk.
findings.expected: One source for each declaration; work done once.
findings.observed: Two pthread_atfork declarations, the page size read twice, two descriptor wrappers, SDDL parsed per thread.
findings.impact: Divergence risk and repeated work.
findings.recommendedFix: Unify them.
findings.requiredVerification: One of each; one parse per walk.

findings.title: The fuzz dependency is not pinned, the notices check misses cases, fuzzing ignores the lockfile
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Read the fuzz manifest, the notices check and the release fuzz step.
findings.expected: Exact pins, a complete check, the lockfile kept.
findings.observed: A range for libfuzzer-sys; a second version on one line and missing packages pass the check; cargo fuzz run has no --locked.
findings.impact: Unreviewed tool versions; stale notices.
findings.recommendedFix: Pin exactly, check both directions, check the lockfile.
findings.requiredVerification: All three in place.

findings.title: Tests miss the start deadline, the process-wide entry, several filter rules and macOS terminals
findings.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
findings.reproduction: Read the tests.
findings.expected: Each new contract has a test.
findings.observed: No test of start_within timing out, enter_requiring_process_wide, migrate_pages, get_robust_list, sched_set*, or other terminals on macOS.
findings.impact: A regression in these paths would pass CI.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the tests.
findings.requiredVerification: The tests exist and pass where they run.

findings.title: Linux enters a user namespace after an unconfirmed dumpable change
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Non-dumpable confirmed before the namespace step.
findings.observed: The prctl answer was discarded before unshare.
findings.impact: Under a policy refusing the prctl, a same-user process could gain inspection rights in the namespace.
findings.recommendedFix: Enter only after a read-back of the cleared flag.
findings.requiredVerification: The namespace step depends on the read-back.

findings.title: The signal option leaves asynchronous terminal signalling outside its check
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Kernel-mediated notifications stay within the process.
findings.observed: O_ASYNC on a terminal makes its foreground group the owner by itself.
findings.impact: Another process group is signalled while SignalsToSelfOnly reads Confirmed.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse new asynchronous notification with the option.
findings.requiredVerification: F_SETSIG and F_SETFL with O_ASYNC refused; tested.

findings.title: Windows can accept or wait for a worker past its deadline
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: The deadline covers the named phases; no late success.
findings.observed: Launch calls ran before the check; the watchdog decided by its channel.
findings.impact: Late success or a longer wait than promised.
findings.recommendedFix: Check expiry before and after; decide by completion time.
findings.requiredVerification: Clock-based decision in within; checks around the launch; narrowed contract.

findings.title: A late Unix launch can leave the child and its waiter alive
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: An abandoned launch is cleaned up.
findings.observed: The launcher waited without ending the child.
findings.impact: A stalled worker and its waiter stay alive.
findings.recommendedFix: End the abandoned child through a stable handle.
findings.requiredVerification: The launcher terminates a child whose start gave up.

findings.title: The file lock option leaves delegated leases available
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Delegations refused with locks.
findings.observed: F_SETDELEG was allowed.
findings.impact: A delegated lease while FileLocksRefused reads Confirmed.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse F_SETDELEG.
findings.requiredVerification: Refused with EACCES; tested.

findings.title: A child of fork keeps the installer's process number in the process rules
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Self-only across fork.
findings.observed: The installer's number was allowed.
findings.impact: A forked child can act on its parent.
findings.recommendedFix: Allow only 0.
findings.requiredVerification: A number is refused; 0 works; tested.

findings.title: The macOS read rule does not exclude every terminal device
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Reads exclude terminal devices but the own one.
findings.observed: Only /dev/ttysN was excluded.
findings.impact: Reading /dev/tty or other terminal devices.
findings.recommendedFix: Exclude every terminal device name.
findings.requiredVerification: tty, pty, cu. and console names excluded.

findings.title: The release checks the fuzz lockfile before a run that can change it
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Fuzz results refer to the checked-in graph.
findings.observed: No check after cargo-fuzz ran.
findings.impact: A changed graph could pass.
findings.recommendedFix: Check the lockfile after the runs.
findings.requiredVerification: git diff --exit-code after fuzzing.

findings.title: The notices check compares partial version strings
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: Exact name and version pairs both ways.
findings.observed: Substring and numeric-triple matching.
findings.impact: A wrong suffix could pass.
findings.recommendedFix: Compare complete pairs.
findings.requiredVerification: Equal sorted pair lists required.

findings.title: The package verification example checks no source commit
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: The example pins the commit.
findings.observed: No --source-digest.
findings.impact: The tag name alone is checked.
findings.recommendedFix: Add --source-digest.
findings.requiredVerification: The example has it.

findings.title: The security policy omits the Windows console boundary
findings.evidence: Static reading by review 4 at its snapshot, with its checks; no exploit was run.
findings.reproduction: See the finding in review 4.
findings.expected: The policy names the console authority a process keeps.
findings.observed: It did not.
findings.impact: Callers may expect console input to be refused.
findings.recommendedFix: Document it.
findings.requiredVerification: SECURITY.md names it.

observations.title: The Windows lock of closed pages is unverified
observations.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
observations.reproduction: Close a locked ClosedSecret on Windows and read its working-set flags.
observations.expected: Its pages stay locked while closed.
observations.impact: Closed secret pages could be paged out.
observations.requiredVerification: A native Windows test of the flags.

observations.title: A new Secret for every frame
observations.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer; no code was run.
observations.observed: Both sides made a new Secret per frame.
observations.impact: System calls and a TLB flush per frame.
observations.requiredVerification: The worker reuses one wiped buffer.

observations.title: A watchdog thread for every Windows read and write
observations.evidence: Static reading by the reviewer at its snapshot, with the checks of review 3.
observations.requiredVerification: One watchdog per call and per start.
